title: Add a Core test seam or scanner-level test for a directory listing that fails partway, then a window case for the tree's 'could not be read in full' row
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: Window case for the tree's 'could not be read in full' row (a folder whose listing failed partway, as opposed to one denied outright): missing

hook-arms-partial-listing-seam-in-published-exe: needs first: A Core-side fault-injection seam keyed by folder path and by how many entries to return before failing (not just SynchronousIoCancel's global per-call error-override counter) would need …

Report shape for the new row state: this design scopes it to what the tree already realizes/visible (matching the existing realizedRows/fullRows granularity) instead of the raw proposal's full row-array with an invented 1000-row truncation cap. A reviewer preferring the fuller dump for future reuse by other tree-shape cases would restore the cap; nothing in this slice's own fixture needs it.
Schema-1 report fields for tree rows (WindowReport.cs). The M2 and m3 dispositions replaced them with tree mode's tree-row lines, and Q-016 keeps row names and figures out of the report.
A Disarm() or IDisposable scope for the failpoint (m7's second half). The disposition did not take it, because only the single hook process arms it in this slice.
FSA_HOOK_TREE_EXPAND. The m6 disposition found that WALK already opens the row.
The failpoint's static state has no disarm (the m7 half that was not taken). If a Core.Tests Fact ever arms it, it would fault parallel tests that list a folder of the same name, so scope it then.

T-008 asserts the runtime's unhandled-exception exit 0xE0434352 for a startup-hook throw. On a machine with WER's UI enabled, a crash dialog could hold the process until the 30 s timeout. It did not happen here, where every launch ended within about a second.

FSA_HOOK_FAIL_LISTING is armed only when FSA_HOOK_MODE is also set, because Initialize returns early without a mode. This is documented in the hook header; a case that sets only the failpoint variable would get an unfaulted scan, but T-007's first check would fail it.
